meta.descripcion: Comprehensive Porsche restoration involving disassembly, documentation, bodywork, mechanical systems, and interiors, all coordinated within a defined scope.

h1: Comprehensive Porsche restoration based on a unique approach

secciones.titulo: Complete Porsche restorations, maintaining the highest level of originality
parrafos: An F-Series 911 with hidden corrosion makes it impossible to finalize the scope of work prior to disassembly.

We restore entire Porsches, aiming for the highest possible degree of originality. Our benchmark is the Porsche Certificate of Authenticity: the document specifying the color, upholstery, and options with which that specific unit left the factory.

A comprehensive restoration is not merely a price quote; it is a conversation. Before dismantling anything, we agree on the project's extent, as the scope determines the outcome and the car's future value.

imagenes.alt: Porsche flat-six stripped down and mounted on the engine stand
Open engine bay of a brown 911, gold fan and manifolds in view
Engine of a 1988 930 Turbo 3.0 in the bay, its gold fan showing under the cover

parrafos: A comprehensive restoration coordinates bodywork, mechanics, electrical systems, interiors, and documentation so that one discipline does not later have to undo a decision made by another.

imagenes.alt: Interior of a restored G-series 911, with beige trim and houndstooth seats
2.2 engine freshly fitted in the bay of a red 1970 F-series 911, with the body on the lift

parrafos: Complete dismantling and cataloging allow us to distinguish between preservation, repair, and replacement. The scope is reviewed when areas are revealed that were not visible while the car was assembled.
The reference point may be the Certificate of Authenticity and the original configuration, although a car intended for frequent use may require different decisions than a collector's unit.

imagenes.alt: Dashboard of a classic 911 with its five dials and four-spoke steering wheel
Dashboard of a red 911 T with the model badge above the glovebox
Complete M64 engine from a 964 on the stand, in the engine room

parrafos: Not all cars require the same approach. For a rare, well-documented unit, originality is paramount, and any deviation detracts from its value. For a car intended for regular use, it makes sense to prioritize reliability—even at the cost of strict factory accuracy—and that is a decision for the owner to make, not us.
What we do not do is start without having had that conversation. Half of the projects that arrive poorly finished from elsewhere started without it.

imagenes.alt: Interior of a restored G-series 911, with beige trim and houndstooth seats
Classic Porsche 911 on the lift with the bonnet open

items: Complete disassembly and cataloging of every part.
Bodywork: sheet metal, anti-corrosion treatment, and painting in original colors.
Engine and transmission, in the engine workshop.
Electrical system, brakes, suspension, and steering.
Sourcing parts—which, for a sixty-year-old car, accounts for half the project.

imagenes.alt: Dashboard of a red 911 T with the model badge above the glovebox
Porsche 964 under a blue cover in the workshop, at the start of a backdating project

parrafos: Below are six restorations detailed step-by-step, featuring photos of the process. Among them are a 911 F-series from 1965—which arrived disassembled in boxes after seven years of being moved around—and a 930 Turbo that arrived following an engine-bay fire.

Brown 1975 Porsche 911 2.7 S on stands in the workshop before restoration

parrafos: The Magazine showcases the work and photos for this documented case.

imagenes.alt: Dark blue Porsche 911 993 from the front three-quarter outside the workshop

parrafos: A rebuilt automobile with an organized record of the process, parts, and decisions, tested as a complete unit before being deemed finished.

imagenes.alt: Dark blue Porsche 911 993 from the front three-quarter outside the workshop
Body of a 1979 911 3.0 SC Targa freshly painted green, masked up in the paint booth

parrafos: Depending on the car's condition and intended use, the work can be coordinated with Porsche restorations, engine work, and body and paint services.

secciones.titulo: Can a full quote be provided before disassembly?
parrafos: An initial scope can be defined, but hidden corrosion and previous repairs can only be accurately assessed once exposed. Any significant findings are presented before expanding the scope of work.
Salvageable original parts linked to the car's identity are prioritized. Safety, wear, and availability determine when repair is no longer a reasonable option.
